title: Time-series KV skew simulator and regression detector for hitrate / p95 / memory
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable load harness that simulates time-varying key skew (hotset drift, diurnal spikes, cold-start flushes) and evaluates the trade-offs between KV/prefix cache hit rate, tail token latency (p95), and memory footprint. The harness should produce deterministic traces (seeded RNG) and a set of derived metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 token latency, cache hit rate over sliding windows (1s, 30s, 5m), memory used by cache structures, eviction rates, prefetch effectiveness, and KV warmup time.

Acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic workload generator supports multiple distributions (Zipfian with changing alpha, bimodal, periodic bursts) and key churn schedules.
- Automated regression detector that raises a signal when p95 increases by >15% with stable load or when hit rate drops >8% relative to baseline, with configurable sensitivity.
- Output artifacts: per-run CSV, annotated flamegraph for p95 tails, dashboard snapshot, and a standardized JSON summary for our CI.
- Harness runs on both single-node (RTX A6000) and multi-shard simulated environments. Baseline seeds and configs checked into repo.

Implementation notes: Use Go harness (existing load-lib) to generate token streams; instrument token-level timing around KV lookup / prefix cache decision. Add lightweight control chart (CUSUM) and bootstrap confidence interval tests for regression detection; keep false positive rate low by requiring sustained deviation for 3 consecutive windows. For memory measurement, sample RSS + internal cache accounting every 500ms and correlate with eviction tallies. Store traces in S3 test-bucket with deterministic path naming.

Trade-offs discussed: We prefer a conservative regression detector (requires multi-window confirmation) to avoid noisy alerts during transient spikes. That increases detection latency but reduces alert fatigue. Chose Go for the harness for lower jitter; analysis scripts in Python for plotting and dashboard ingestion.

Next steps: wire CI job (nightly), add GitHub Actions with artifact upload, and author onboarding doc.
